title: Indian Content Hits 688 Million Views on Netflix in Six Months, Ranking Third Globally Behind Only the US and UK
excerpt: Netflix's latest engagement report reveals India is now the top contributor to non-English film viewing worldwide, with titles like Dhurandhar, Accused and Made in Korea entering the global top charts.
body:
• Indian titles generated 688 million views on Netflix between January and June 2026, marking a record-breaking half-year for Indian content on the platform.
  • India is now the number one contributor to non-English film viewing on Netflix globally and ranks third overall for film viewing, behind only the United States and United Kingdom.
  • Four Indian films entered the Global Top 100, led by Dhurandhar with 37 million views — the most-watched Indian film on Netflix during the period.
  • Made in Korea became the first South Indian film to reach number one on Netflix's Global Non-English Films chart.

India's Streaming Moment Arrives

Netflix's What We Watched report for January through June 2026, released on July 17, paints a striking picture of Indian content's global reach. Indian films, series, unscripted shows and creator-led entertainment collectively logged 688 million views in the first half of the year — a figure that places India as the platform's third-largest market for film viewing worldwide, trailing only the United States and United Kingdom.

The milestone represents more than a statistical achievement. India has become the single largest source of non-English film content on Netflix, overtaking markets like South Korea and Japan that had previously dominated that space. The shift reflects both the growing scale of Indian production on the platform and a widening international appetite for Indian storytelling.

Dhurandhar Leads the Charge

At the center of the surge is Dhurandhar, the Ranveer Singh-starrer spy actioner directed by Aditya Dhar, which amassed 37 million views to become the most-watched Indian film on Netflix during the reporting period. The film's box office success — the Dhurandhar franchise has grossed over ₹3,000 crore worldwide — translated directly to streaming dominance.

Three other Indian films joined it in the Global Top 100: Accused, a Konkona Sensharma-led thriller that trended in 74 countries; Made in Korea; and Mardaani 3. Netflix Originals performed particularly well, with five titles — Accused, Made in Korea, Kartavya, Maa Behen and Toaster — reaching the Global Top 500.

"Made in Korea became the first South Indian film to reach number one on Netflix's Global Non-English Films chart at the time of its release."

— Netflix What We Watched Report, January–June 2026

Series Break Through Across Genres

Indian series showed equally strong momentum. Taskaree: The Smuggler's Web became India's highest-ranked series ever on the Global Top 100 TV List, a benchmark no Indian show had previously reached. Five other Indian series made the Global Top 500: Desi Bling, Maamla Legal Hai, India's Got Latent, Glory and Kohrra.

The Great Indian Kapil Show, now in its fourth season, continued to demonstrate the international appeal of Indian comedy and unscripted entertainment, becoming the second most-viewed Indian series on Netflix by viewing hours. Separately, Ormax Media's mid-year streaming report showed that India's Got Latent Season 2, hosted by comedian Samay Raina, topped all OTT content in India with 38.5 million viewers — surpassing even Dhurandhar despite ongoing legal controversies surrounding the show.

The Business Behind the Numbers

Netflix's investment in Indian content has been building for years, but the scale of the payoff in the first half of 2026 is unprecedented. The platform has moved beyond licensing Bollywood hits to commissioning a broad slate of originals spanning Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada languages. The diversity of the content breaking through globally — from big-budget action franchises to intimate thrillers to regional comedies — suggests that the audience for Indian stories is not confined to the diaspora.

For the Indian film industry, the data validates a long-held thesis: that quality Indian content can compete globally when given proper distribution. The fact that a South Indian film reached number one on the non-English chart is particularly significant, as it demonstrates that linguistic barriers within India's own fragmented market are less relevant on a global streaming platform.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs scattered across time zones, Netflix has become the primary way to stay connected with Indian popular culture. The platform's global reach means that new releases are available simultaneously worldwide, eliminating the delays that once left diaspora audiences weeks or months behind. The strong performance of Indian content on global charts also carries cultural weight — it signals that the stories Indians grew up with are finding resonance far beyond their traditional audiences.
